title: Add JSON Schema response_format with strict validation and OpenAI-compat mapping
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds first-class support for response_format: {type: "json_schema", schema: <JSON Schema>, strict: <bool>} across the Redwood API and OpenAI-compat layer. Motivation: customers need deterministic structured outputs and clear errors when generation violates an expected schema. This PR implements validation at the platform boundary, a strict mode that turns schema violations into deterministic errors, streaming-friendly partial validation heuristics, OpenAI-compatibility mapping for the /v1/completions and chat endpoints, and comprehensive tests and docs. Checklist: [x] core response_format plumbing and runtime hooks, [x] JSON Schema validator and error canonicalization, [x] strict mode enforcement with clear error codes, [x] OpenAI-compat parameter parsing and error mapping, [x] streaming compatibility (best-effort partial validation + final enforcement), [x] unit + integration tests, [x] docs + examples. See related design notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4213/json-schema-response-format and compatibility notes in docs/openai-compat.md.
commits: Initial implementation of response_format parsing and wiring
Add JSON Schema validator and error canonicalization layer
Integrate strict-mode enforcement into response pipeline with fallback behavior
OpenAI-compat: map response_format and error codes for /v1 endpoints
Streaming: add partial validation heuristics and tests
Add unit and integration tests + CI fixes
review_comments: Daniel Ortiz: Left a few nits on naming (ResponseFormat vs response_format) and suggested extracting the OpenAI mapping into a small adapter — addressed in follow-up commit.

Priya Nair: Requested clearer semantics for strict=true (should it always return 4xx or offer best-effort?) — added explicit behavior: strict=true => platform returns structured validation error (400-like) and can include the model output in debug mode; documented tradeoffs.

Liam O'Connor: Noted risk around streaming where partial JSON fragments can incorrectly trigger validation failures — implemented partial_validator heuristics and added tests showing no false positives for short fragments.
Maya Chen (author): Responded to comments, clarified the error shape, and added canonical error codes to match OpenAI-compat mapping (code: "invalid_schema", message: ...).
release_notes: Feature: response_format="json_schema" - allow customers to supply a JSON Schema to validate model outputs.
Feature: strict mode - when strict=true the platform returns a validation error if the final model output fails schema validation.
Compatibility: OpenAI-compat layer now accepts response_format and maps validation errors to OpenAI-style error responses.
Behavior: streaming uses best-effort partial validation to avoid noisy failures; final enforcement occurs on completion unless strict=false where best-effort corrected outputs may be returned.
Docs and examples added for Python/TS SDKs.
